name: Saint Paul
biography: Credited with the decisive move of admitting gentiles to Christianity without requiring circumcision or the Mosaic Law, thereby making Christianity capable of becoming a universal religion; also shown warning against 'philosophy and vain deceit' despite his own use of Greek cultural references.
central_doctrines: The Pauline admission of gentiles: The Pauline policy, contested by James and Peter, of admitting gentile converts to the Christian community without requiring circumcision or submission to the Mosaic Law, retaining Judaism's attractive features (moral certainty, sacred history) while removing the obstacles (circumcision, dietary law) that had limited its spread among gentiles.
